⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5 – Authentic Malvani Taste at Its Best!

Visited Malvani Klub Restaurant at Lalbaugh with my wife, and we were genuinely impressed with the food, service, and overall experience. We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

The Bangda fry in the thali had that perfect Malvani masala flavour, and the curries were rich, aromatic, and truly reminded us of homely Maharashtrian coastal food. The prawns curry was equally flavourful, and the chapatis were soft and fresh.

Apart from the excellent food, the staff deserves a special mention — very polite, friendly, and attentive. They made the dining experience even better with their warm hospitality.

If you love Maharashtrian or Malvani cuisine, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Every dish has a homely yet rich taste that leaves you wanting to try more.
The atmosphere is lively and comfortable perfect for families or groups. The interiors have a simple, rustic charm and the overall vibe makes you feel right at home. What really impressed me was the staff they’re extremely polite, attentive, and always ready to suggest the best dishes based on your taste.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.name: Subodh Mishra
featured_reviews.review_text:
While Juhu is famous for its beach snacks and high-end cafes, the real magic happens in the kitchens that treat seafood with the respect it deserves. This isn't just a meal; it’s a deep dive into the culinary traditions of the Konkan coast.
The Ambiance
Don't expect minimalist chic. The vibe here is "busy Sunday lunch." It’s loud, efficient, and smells heavenly. The decor is usually simple because the owners know you aren't there to look at the walls—you’re there for the crab.
The Standout Dishes
Bombil Fry (Bombay Duck): A local must-have. It’s light, crisp on the outside, and melts like butter the moment it hits your tongue. If it doesn't crunch, it's not authentic.
Butter Garlic Pepper Crab: This is the messiest, most rewarding dish on the menu. The meat is succulent, and the sauce is so rich you’ll want to mop it up with a Neer Dosa.
Surmai (Kingfish) Thali: For the solo diner or the traditionalist. A thick, spicy masala fry served alongside a bowl of soul-warming Sol Kadhi (a pink, tangy coconut milk appetizer).
The Verdict
The service is brisk—they expect you to eat, enjoy, and make room for the next hungry patron. It’s a bit pricey compared to street food, but for the freshness of the catch, it’s worth every rupee.
Pro Tip: Always ask for the "Catch of the Day" before looking at the menu. If the Pomfret is fresh, don't overthink it—just order it.

We ordered crab garlic, surmai garlic masala, bombil thecha fry, surmai green masala, rice with plain fish curry, solkadi and lime soda. The only real savior in the entire meal was the surmai green masala. The solkadi and lime soda were fine.

Everything else was a letdown. The fish curry had no tanginess, no salt, no flavour. It tasted flat and unfinished. For a seafood restaurant, getting a basic fish curry wrong is shocking. The crab garlic and bombil thecha fry were also disappointing.

I even called the waiter and asked him to taste the fish curry himself. He did not argue or defend it. He was so sure I was right that he did not even attempt to try it.

Service was good and the waiter was polite and attentive. But good service cannot save bad food.

Prices are high, but the taste does not justify it at all. Very disappointing experience. Would not return.

The place has a G+2 seating arrangement—non-AC on the ground floor and AC seating on the first and second floors. Seating is decent.

Unlike many traditional bars, no complimentary chakna is served here. Alcohol prices felt on the higher side, and the 180 ml vodka was served from a larger container instead of a sealed bottle, which was a bit disappointing. Mixers were limited to Coke and Sprite only. Coming to food: Apple Chicken was good, and the green kokani/malvani-style kairi chutney served with it was unique and delicious. We ordered Chicken Thali (₹300) and Mutton Thali (₹430). featured_reviews.name: The explorer
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a rather shockingly disappointing experience during a Sunday Brunch. Not only was the vegetarian menu bizarre and short but the dishes were also placed in between multiple non vegetarian dishes or under them in a dark shelf.

Delving into the vegetarian food cuisine-wise:

The chaat counter - unimpressed with the paste like aaloo tikki chaat served with some gugni and loads of sev poured on it with lack of any depth in flavor/texture. Extremely disappointed after waiting and following up for this dish. The mini samosas were really good though. Ram ki laddu - cold & hard.

Sushi - couple of veg options that tasted okay. No soy sauce found adjacent to it.

Mediterranean - hummus, muhammara, labneh, fattoush salad placed next to the chaat counter. But the pita breads/falafel are nowhere to be found. So, one's supposed to eat hummus alone?

Similarly, the veg appetizers doodhiya paneer tikka, kasundi broccoli were well done but lacked any accompaniments nearby. The green chutney was to be served after travelling to the litti chokha station.!

Litti chokha, chole bhature, thalipeeth, mushroom soup, and the live counter soups (manchow, clear) were again okay but nothing to write home about. Chole bhature are ofcourse playing hide&seek behind a few non veg dishes. Maa ki Dal was alone thrown in the middle of multiple non veg dishes that we couldn't locate it the first time.

Upon a lot of rigorous treasure hunt did we find another dal/curry near thalipeeth and a stuffed brinjal curry dispersed someplace else.

Hence finding north Indian veg food was nothing short of an adventure.

And yes, we had to request for steamed rice, roti, pulao and mix veg curry to actually make a meal ourselves. The veg pulao that they offered (as veg menu was short & lacking), was a tawa pulao which was on the spicier side. They were kind enough to send a couple of veg curries (paneer and mix veg) which tasted delicious but the roti/rice lacked in quality to complement them.

Italian - veg Ratatouille, veg puff with spinach corn filling (but is unnamed at the counter) are the italian offerings. Pasta was only made in non veg and we had to ask for a veg preparation of pasta to be made that tasted mediocre again.

Missing cuisines that are quite common in other buffets - thai, mexican,south Indian. thai veg curry with Jasmine rice, some nachos with salsa/guacamole are the highly anticipated ones in buffets in general and are offered in most of them.

Hence the food and Savory were a serious let down in multiple aspects.

The desserts however were a solace and the only savior after choosing this brunch. The array of full cakes, pound/bar cakes, the chocolate barks, Indian desserts, sorbet, DIY sago pudding, ukadiche modak, affogato, icecreams and entremets had variety and quality. The mocktails served as a part of the menu were also well made and are great thirst quenchers.

Therefore this meal was all about having sweet treats with your loved ones while enjoying the live music.

There was also a bangle making counter that made bangles for the female guests upon request and this was a highly unique offering in a brunch.

As a part of mother's day, rose flowers/ Jasmine garlands (gajra) could be taken

The food, in all its courses was underwhelming for vegetarians.
Also, respecting the fact that it would be less confusing and comfortable to place all the vegetarian dishes to one side or have their veg/nonveg highlighting name plate would greatly help alleviate the experience.

Service: Highly uncoordinated, create a noisy environment with their mutual communication and always appearing to be on the run. The requests placed at live counter weren't honoured and needed follow ups. Staff would stand in the way (of an already narrow & congested pathway) to discuss among themselves or manager disciplining the crew right infront of a dessert counter. Some of the staff at serving counters seemed indifferent to a question asked and lacked basic warmth. Overall, service needs alot of improvement and  be more welcoming, warm and attentive towards the guests.

featured_reviews.name: Pereira Gynel
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has such an amazing tropical ambience. You are welcomed by soulful Goan music, and the vibe is relaxed and unhurried. The servers don’t rush you, making it a perfect spot to truly enjoy your meal.

Mr. Merwin, the manager, took great care of us, and our servers Sonia and Edwin were humble, polite, and very prompt, obliging us with every request.

The food is unlike anything you’ve tasted.. authentic Goan cuisine rooted deeply in the culture and spices of Goa. Every dish is beautifully presented, with thoughtful plating that elevates the experience without being overdone. The cutlery, plates, and glassware are aesthetically pleasing and enhance the dining experience, without robbing you of quantity. Portions are generous and satisfying.

From the big plates, we had the Traditional Pork Sorpatel with rice, Goan-style chilli chicken, and Surmai fish curry rice. The sorpatel was so authentic it made my mum emotional...it brought back memories of old friends who had cooked traditional pork dishes in her younger days. The Goan-style chilli chicken was the standout dish of the afternoon...smooth, succulent, and packed with a powerful flavour punch. The surmai fish curry rice felt like something an old granny had made, warm, comforting, and soulful.

From the small plates, we tried the Goan fried chicken with spicy mayo...six generous boneless strips, made to order, pairing perfectly with lime and the spicy mayo. The grilled squid stuffed with crab was outstanding, with the masala truly stealing the show. The prawn balchao masala stuffed forminhas crispy tarts were tangy and well-made; while not my personal favourite, they were only overshadowed by stronger dishes. The tender coconut and raw mango salad was light, tropical, refreshing, and beautifully balanced.

For drinks, we had the Coconut Boy Refresher, Kokum Spritz, and Tamarind Trails. These are not your usual cocktails... Goan spices and flavours take centre stage, and an open mind is needed to fully enjoy them.

Coconut Boy truly lives up to its promise of 'fresh' and delivers an experience that transports you straight to Goa. Highly recommended even if you’re simply looking for some relaxed downtime with exceptional food and service.

featured_reviews.name: Everything On A Plate EOAP
featured_reviews.review_text:
AMBIENCE:

Despite being located at a busy intersection, the instant you come inside, you are taken to a tranquil and unexpectedly quiet environment. Amidst the dim lights and décor paying ode to the Goan theme, what we appreciated the most was the ample open space to move around and even dance (which our daughter did multiple times throughout the night).

FOOD:
Vegetable Cheese Rissois: Though the classic Portuguese fried pastry is usually filled with meat, we tried the vegetarian version and were not disappointed. It starts with a crumbly-soft bite which leads to a minced vegetables mixed with cheese that definitely melts in your mouth.

Mapusa Market toast with Cheese & Green Chilli: Coconut boys take on the chilli cheese toast with a twist. On first look it’s just your average cheese chilli toast, but one bite into it and you hit a tangy punch which took us by surprise…. It was mango aachaar! ‘Who would’ave thunk?’ This dish did have some mixed opinions!

Choris Chilli Fry: Choriz tossed with chilli, onion, tomato teamed up with warm, fluffy poee… we absolutely left licking our fingers. Would have gone for round two but there was more to be relished on the menu.

Grilled Squid Stuffed with Crab: A host suggestion that we absolutely jumped at the mention of! Crab meat tossed in Recheado, stuffed into a squid & grilled… a lot of effort goes into this. Hints of spice married with the sweetness of the crab meat and the bite of squid… a messy meal you must try at least once! Definitely big brownie points for the squid NOT being chewy.

Mushroom & vegetables slow cooked with Xacuti masala: A medley of steamed veggies (Mushroom, carrot, potato, cauliflower) tossed in a Xacuti gravy. You have an option of Poee or steamed rice to accompany it and we went with the latter. We requested them to hold back the spice a bit for our toddler & it’s wholesome, earthy, slightly-sweet coconut-ty broth was welcomed with a smack of the lips.

Serradura: This simple pudding can go awry in so many ways… And believe me, we've tasted some absolute disasters. But coconut boy absolutely nailed-it! The crumbly, biscuit dust alternated with fluffy, light whipped cream was what we devoured at the end of a great meal. Not too sweet, not too dense… just perfect.

Service: The service undoubtedly elevated our entire experience! We had Siddhesh giving us amazing recommendations and making sure we had everything we needed. Akbar stopped by with some fantastic banter, and last but not least, Faustin, whom our daughter adored and sat with virtually the entire dinner, allowing us to savour every bite!

SUMMING UP: If you love Goan food, it’s definitely an experience you do not want to miss. Right from the décor to the service, it’s comfy, cozy and warm. The cost is a bit on the higher end but the quality and flavors are worth every penny.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Our family has enjoyed dinner here. Authentic kokani taste. Wada, bhakari, modak, chicken, kala vatanyachi usal everything was tasty.
Place is nice and since it was Thursday it was less crowded as people think kokani food means nonveg only.
Ambience is good, interior is good well decorated.
Wash room is clean but very small and entering inside washroom will be difficult for an oversized person so management should do something about it, also the flash tank does not get filled quickly after someone use washroom.
